title: One bigger project split into parallel parts, looped until green
persona: A senior engineer who likes things done properly but types very little. Expects the AI to organize the work itself.
goals: Get a tiny key-value store built in a folder named kvstore: a python library module (get/set/delete/keys, persisted to a JSON file), a command-line interface on top of it, and a small HTTP server (python standard library http.server) exposing GET/PUT/DELETE /kv/<key>, each with pytest tests.
It should be split into parts worked on in parallel, not done by one session in sequence.
Everything must end with the whole test suite passing; you want main to keep looping until it does.
script: Give the whole request in one or two messages and say it can be split up and done in parallel.
Wait for main to come back. If it reports partial progress, tell it to keep going until all tests pass.
At the end ask how many tests there are and whether they all pass.

checks.name: kvstore tests pass
checks.cmd: cd kvstore && python3 -m pytest -q >/tmp/pytest.$$.out 2>&1 && echo PYTEST-OK || tail -5 /tmp/pytest.$$.out

checks.name: kvstore has cli + server
checks.cmd: cd kvstore && grep -rlE 'http.server|HTTPServer' . --include=*.py | head -2 && grep -rlE 'argparse|sys.argv' . --include=*.py | head -2
